name: Apply ESOI to a project
scoped_purpose: Use for turning a project's intent into specifications that are checked, measured and selected by metric, and for keeping the structure evolving with the intent. It avoids saying what the project is for: that is the project's own top intent.
goals: A person or an agent can specify an intent, compare the alternatives of each solution by metric and let the best one be used, with every part reachable from the specifications.
knowledge: The author's skill: its definitions, the intent specification, the five specification templates and the principles; the adopters' experience.
measures_of_success: A newcomer applies ESOI from the documents alone with few questions, and a project's records pass the structure check.
parameters: The project's own top intent, and which implementations of the building blocks to use.
inputs: A project's intent, in its owner's words.
outputs: Specifications for the project (an intent folder with its five record types), checks and metric results.
effects: None beyond the files the project keeps.
usage_notes: Start from the documents and templates; add the Python tools where checks, measurement and selection should run by themselves.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: with the tools the records are checked and the best implementation is selected by metric (principle 4), where documents only leave both to the reader
gap: No recorded trial compares the adoption effort of the two implementations, so the choice rests on principle 4, not on a measurement.
action: Have a newcomer apply ESOI to a fresh repository once documents only and once with the tools, and record each as a run of metric-adoption-effort; review this by 2026-12-31.

name: Intent registry
scoped_purpose: Use for recording every problem, solution, implementation, ideal and metric of a repository as linked records that people and checks both read. Avoids holding results (those belong to the results log) and avoids prose design documents.
goals: Every intent item is one record with every template field filled; every link resolves both ways; every file reaches a solution through the ownership map.
knowledge: The intent template in the evolvable-structure skill; Joshua's Project Documentation board (solution definitions apart from implementations); requirements traceability practice.
measures_of_success: A reader can follow any file to its problem and ideal, and every record is complete.
parameters: The template's fields per type.
inputs: Hand-edited records of each type, the ownership map.
outputs: A linked intent network that the check, the tracker and the selection read.
usage_notes: Add or edit a record before building a new capability; the check names anything missing.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A record is complete and linked or it is not; the cases pin what the check must keep.

name: Template sync
scoped_purpose: Use for deriving the registry's fields from the intent template in the skill, so the author's wording is the only definition. Avoids adding fields of its own or interpreting the template.
goals: The registry's fields equal the template's fields after every refinement.
knowledge: The skill's `SKILL.md` as the source of truth; derived-copy practice already used for the standing instructions.
measures_of_success: A template refinement shows up as named missing fields on the next check, with no hand edit of any schema.
parameters: Path to the skill.
inputs: The skill's intent template.
outputs: A committed field list per type.
effects: Fails the check when the committed field list is stale.
usage_notes: Run after Joshua edits the template; public CI, which cannot read the skill, checks records against the committed list.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A field is read the same way or it is not; the cases pin the reading rules.

name: Ownership map
scoped_purpose: Use for assigning every file to exactly one component and every component to the solutions it serves. Avoids describing what the code does (the solution records do that).
goals: No file unowned, no component serving nothing, no module past the size ceiling, imports pointing inward.
knowledge: Layered and hexagonal architecture; code owners practice; the repository's split rule.
measures_of_success: Code that serves no solution is found and removed.
parameters: Layer order, size ceiling.
inputs: The file tree and the component records.
outputs: File-to-solution links and the generated component index.
usage_notes: A new file joins a component in the same change; a file that fits no solution is a sign the code should go.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A file has one owner and an import points inward or it does not.

name: Implementation selection
scoped_purpose: Use for choosing which implementation serves a swappable solution by name, configuration or table default. Avoids deciding which one is best (the leaderboard does) and avoids per-call branching.
goals: Switching is a data change; an unknown name fails with the choices; every listed implementation loads.
knowledge: Ports and adapters; plugin registries; lazy loading of optional dependencies.
measures_of_success: Every switch works from configuration alone and no typo falls back silently.
parameters: Solution id, implementation name, configuration overrides.
inputs: The selection table.
outputs: The chosen implementation's class and its configuration type.
usage_notes: Every solution with a port has a table entry whose default equals the measured winner or a declared tie.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No run measures this solution itself: its chosen implementation is measured through runtime-selection in the esoi-runtime intent, and its rival (entry-point plugins) is not built or recorded.
action: Build the entry-point rival and record a run of both on the selection cases, or drop the rival from the alternatives; review by 2026-12-31.

name: Measurement harness
scoped_purpose: Use for running each implementation of a solution against that solution's cases through the live code and recording the result with its provenance. Avoids ranking and avoids tests that only check code runs.
goals: Every eval solution has cases, a scorer and implementations that drive shipped code; every recorded result carries its commit, case hash, cost and tokens; a call budget stops a run.
knowledge: Evaluation practice for language models (held-out cases, staged sample sizes, judged rubrics); experiment tracking; the eval ladder of three, ten and thirty cases.
measures_of_success: Any result can be rerun from its record, and no result was produced by code other than what ships.
parameters: Solution, implementation, case subset, call budget.
inputs: Case files, the implementation, any live services the cases need.
outputs: A results row per run.
effects: Model spend on live runs; refuses to run against production.
usage_notes: Start live runs small and stop at the budget; re-record on committed code after any change to measured code or cases.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A record carries its provenance and a budget is enforced, or it does not.

name: Leaderboard
scoped_purpose: Use for deciding, from recorded results, which implementation of a solution is best or whether they tie. Avoids running anything and avoids comparing results from different case sets.
goals: A win is called only outside the noise margin; ties, losses and unmeasured arms are labelled as such; comparison-only arms are never rivals.
knowledge: Statistical noise in small judged samples; cost and token accounting; Pareto comparison of quality and cost.
measures_of_success: Its verdicts match known rankings on pinned cases and never call a tie a win.
parameters: Noise margin and spend tolerance per component.
inputs: The results log.
outputs: A verdict per solution and a ranked board.
usage_notes: The check requires the selected implementation to be the winner or a declared tie with a reason.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A verdict is right for a result set or it is not.

name: Discriminating cases
scoped_purpose: Use for proving that a solution's cases can tell a sound implementation from a naive one, especially for rules where best cannot vary. Avoids inventing rivals that exist only to lose a comparison.
goals: Every invariant solution has at least one naive baseline that fails its cases.
knowledge: Mutation testing; the gap between a passing test and a meaningful one.
measures_of_success: No case set passes everything that is put in front of it.
parameters: None.
inputs: A solution's cases and its naive baselines.
outputs: A pass or fail per baseline.
usage_notes: Write the naive version a first draft would produce, not a deliberately silly one.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No run reports how many invariant solutions have a naive baseline that fails their cases; one test proves each baseline individually.
action: Record the share over the invariant solutions as a run of metric-case-discrimination; review by 2026-12-31.

name: Structure check
scoped_purpose: Use for enforcing every structural rule on each change, before commit and in tests. Avoids judging code quality beyond the rules, and avoids rules no one can fix.
goals: Every rule violation is reported by rule and path; a clean tree passes; strict mode refuses results from uncommitted code; an exception lives only as a waiver with a reason that disappears when it stops applying.
knowledge: Architecture tests and linters; the repository's numbered rules; the leaderboard (reused, not copied).
measures_of_success: Every injected violation is caught, nothing clean is flagged, and it runs fast enough that nobody skips it.
parameters: Strict mode.
inputs: The repository, the registry, the results log, the waivers.
outputs: A list of violations and an exit code.
effects: Blocks a commit or a test run that breaks a rule.
usage_notes: Add a rule when a mistake has happened twice; delete a rule that stops catching anything.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A violation is reported by the right rule or it is not.

name: Review tracker
scoped_purpose: Use for putting the whole intent network and its current results in front of a human reviewer, and carrying their edits back. Avoids being a second source of truth for anything but review columns.
goals: Every record and its latest verdict appears in one sheet; reviewer edits survive rebuilds and flow back to the repository.
knowledge: Spreadsheets as the team's review medium; two-way sync keyed by record id.
measures_of_success: Joshua can make and record every review decision from the sheet.
parameters: Which tabs, which columns a reviewer may edit.
inputs: The registry and the results log.
outputs: Generated tracker tables and the synced sheet.
usage_notes: Rebuild after any registry or result change; the check fails when the tracker is stale.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A tab follows the registry and keeps reviewers' notes or it does not.

name: Consumer check
scoped_purpose: Use for letting a system built on a library record which library solution each of its parts serves, score its own implementations with the library's cases, and see its version lag. Avoids copying the library's checks into the consumer and avoids putting the consumer's private data in the library.
goals: Every integration point maps to a library solution; every consumer store is scored by the library's cases; the pin's lag is visible.
knowledge: Consumer-driven contract testing; the library's own structure check and cases.
measures_of_success: The consumer passes with nothing unmapped, unscored or unexplained.
parameters: The consumer's registry, root, requirements, solutions and results files; whether lag fails.
inputs: The consumer repository.
outputs: Violations and notes.
usage_notes: Run in the consumer's tests; bump the pin after the library's changes land.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A drifted integration is caught or it is not.

name: The standard
scoped_purpose: Use for teaching anyone, person or AI, how a solution is shaped in this structure and how another repository adopts it. Avoids repeating what the checks already enforce.
goals: One document gives the shape of a solution end to end and the steps to adopt it elsewhere.
knowledge: the adopting repositories as worked examples; the evolvable-structure skill.
measures_of_success: Someone following it alone reaches a passing check.
parameters: None.
inputs: The registry's rules and examples.
outputs: The standard document.
usage_notes: Read first; update in the same change as any rule.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No newcomer trial of following only the standard has been recorded.
action: Have a newcomer follow only the standard in a fresh repository and record the effort as a run of metric-adoption-effort; review by 2026-12-31.

name: Structure budget
scoped_purpose: Use for keeping the structure's own cost in view and pruning what stops paying. Avoids removing rules that still catch real mistakes.
goals: The effort the structure adds to a change is known, and rules, records and checks that catch nothing are removed.
knowledge: Principle 12 (minimalism) and the skill's difficulties; developer-experience research.
measures_of_success: Small changes stay small and every rule has caught something real.
parameters: None yet.
inputs: The check's history, time per check, files touched per change.
outputs: A periodic report of cost against catches.
usage_notes: Not built yet; this record holds the place so the cost is not forgotten.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No run measures the structure's cost against the violations it catches; the written weighing rule is applied by people.
action: Record the time the check adds and the real violations it caught over a month, and decide whether a coded implementation pays; review by 2026-12-31.

name: When metrics are run
scoped_purpose: Use for deciding when each Metric is run, in what stages, with what limit, who approves the spend, and when its result stops counting. Avoids deciding how a metric is implemented or which alternative is best.
goals: Offline metrics run on every change; paid metrics run only when a decision depends on them, in staged samples inside a budget; every recorded result can be told current from stale.
knowledge: Evaluation practice for models (staged and stratified samples, call budgets, noise); continuous integration practice; the cost of re-running against the cost of deciding wrongly.
measures_of_success: Decisions are backed by current results, spend is approved and proportionate, and stale results are found at the change rather than at a release.
parameters: Trigger: every change for the offline metrics, in the test suite and in continuous integration; a paid metric only when a decision depends on it, in staged samples inside a call budget and with Joshua's approval.
inputs: The committed code, the case files and the results log.
outputs: A row per run in the results log with the commit and the hash of the cases; the strict check's verdict.
effects: Offline metrics call no paid service and no network; a paid metric calls a model only when it is run on a decision. Re-recording changes only the results log.
usage_notes: After changing measured code or cases, commit, then run `esoi run --stale`, then commit the results.
selected_by: the only implementation built
invariant_reason: A result is called stale or current correctly, or it is not; the cases pin the rules.

name: Skill distribution
scoped_purpose: Use for publishing an author's skill from the private folder where it is maintained, as a complete public folder that people install without the rest. Avoids deciding what the skill says (the author's own file does) and avoids hosting.
goals: The public copy always equals what the source generates, nothing private is in it, and installing it is one step in each of three ways.
knowledge: The skill's own layout (one authoritative file and supporting notes); plugin and skill folder conventions of the agents that read them; derived-copy practice used for the intent template.
measures_of_success: After any edit of the source, a check names exactly what is stale; a planted private term, path or email is always caught; a fresh install equals the published copy.
parameters: The source folder, the include list, the substitutions, the list of private terms.
inputs: The author's skill folder and a list of private terms that is never published.
outputs: A public skill folder, a plugin manifest and marketplace file, and an installed copy.
effects: Writes the public folders; fails the check on a stale copy or a leak; an install writes into a skills folder.
usage_notes: Run the sync after the source changes and commit the result; run the check in a place that can see the source and the private terms; people install with the plugin, a download or the command.
selected_by: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
invariant_reason: A copy is current and clean or it is not; the cases pin what the sync and the check must keep.

name: ESOI applied to AI behaviour
scoped_purpose: Use for making an AI agent act by the evolvable-structure principles in its own work (designing, building, writing and advising), and for choosing between the ways of giving it those principles. Avoids deciding what the principles say (the author's skill does) and avoids judging an agent's general ability.
goals: Cases cover every principle, including cases where the right behaviour is to hold back or to keep a qualifier; each way of giving the agent the principles is measured on the same cases; the instructions in use are the measured winner or a declared tie; the closing summary of every use says how the principles were applied.
knowledge: The author's skill and its principles, especially principle 4 (humans need only review metrics, not implementations, though they can still add value to implementations) and principle 7 (perspectives are implementations); evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, staged samples, a no-instructions baseline); practice for loading skills and standing instructions.
measures_of_success: The share of cases where the agent's reply acts by the principle, per principle, compared with the same agent without the instructions, with restraint and kept-qualifier cases counted as often as build cases.
parameters: The model, the way the principles are given (standing instructions, on request, none), the case subset and a call budget.
inputs: A task prompt an agent might be sent.
outputs: The agent's reply and, for a judged run, a verdict with a reason.
effects: A live measurement calls a model and costs money; nothing else.
usage_notes: Run the offline checks on every change; run a live arm only when a decision depends on it and the spend is approved (structure/metric-run-policy.md). A person who corrects an agent's behaviour adds or edits a case, not only the instructions, so the correction is measured from then on.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: The metric is carried out by behave-by-esoi, whose arms that call a model have no recorded run yet, so the ways of giving an agent the principles are not ranked.
action: On Joshua's approval, run the staged sample of the model arms under the metric run policy and let the leaderboard rank them; review by 2026-12-31.

name: The ESOI steps
scoped_purpose: Use for the order in which to define and apply ESOI to anything new or changed, and for where to loop back when something changes. Avoids restating what each record type asks (the template does) and avoids prescribing tools.
goals: Every principle is carried out by at least one step; human steps are marked; metrics and their checks come before implementations; the process names how it is itself improved.
knowledge: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist; the author's skill (definitions, intent template, principles); trials of people and agents applying the steps.
measures_of_success: Trials complete the steps without asking what comes next, with no silent skips, and end with a passing check and a checked metric.
parameters: The size of the work (a sentence per step for a small change, full records for a project) and the next milestone that sets how much structure pays for itself.
inputs: An intent stated by a person.
outputs: Linked records, a checked metric, measured implementations and a recorded selection; a short summary of how the steps were applied.
usage_notes: Read skill/evolvable-structure/steps.md; the one-hour guide is a short first pass through it. Record a trial whenever someone follows the steps, and change the steps when a trial shows a confusing, skipped or missing step.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No trial of a person or an agent following the steps is recorded, so the steps are not compared with the other orders.
action: Have a newcomer and an agent each follow the steps on real work and record each trial as a run of metric-steps-followed; review by 2026-12-31.

name: Documentation and templates
scoped_purpose: Use for explaining ESOI and giving fill-in templates that need no code, so anyone can apply it by hand first. Avoids restating the author's template in other words.
goals: A newcomer can write an overall network and a first solution from the templates alone.
knowledge: The skill's definitions, principles and intent template, quoted.
measures_of_success: Someone following the guides alone reaches a passing check.
parameters: None.
inputs: The skill's SKILL.md.
outputs: Explanations, guides and generated templates.
usage_notes: Read the explanation first, then copy a template.
selected_by: the only implementation built
invariant_reason: The documentation is one set with no rival implementation to rank.
gap: No recorded run measures how a newcomer fares with the documentation.
action: Have a newcomer follow the guides in a fresh repository and record the effort as a run.

name: Follow the steps
scoped_purpose: Use for the written order in which to define and apply ESOI, as shipped in the public skill and the guides. Avoids restating the intent template and avoids tooling.
goals: The steps file ships in every copy of the skill, the guides point to it, and each trial of following it is recorded.
knowledge: The 2020 Project Documentation board checklist; the author's skill.
measures_of_success: Trials complete the steps without asking what comes next and with no silent skips.
parameters: None.
inputs: The skill's steps.md.
outputs: The steps in the public skill and the guides that point to them.
usage_notes: Edit steps.md in the author's skill and run `esoi skill sync`; never edit the copy here.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: the steps are the only implementation that carries out every principle, and the choice stands until a recorded trial shows another does better
invariant_reason: No recorded trial exists yet to rank the steps against the one-hour pass; the gap and action say how one will.
gap: No trial of a person or an agent following the steps has been recorded.
action: Have a newcomer and an agent each follow the steps on a real piece of work and record the trial as metric-steps-followed describes.

name: Local ESOI index
scoped_purpose: Use for finding which projects on this machine or board ESOI is applied to, how they relate and where to look first in each, from the person's own index. It avoids holding anything about a project beyond a pointer and its relations: the project's own records stay in the project.
goals: A question about where to look is answered for any listed project, including one added later, and for a path outside every project the answer is none.
knowledge: How the folder for a tool's user settings works in other tools; the principle of finding and reusing structure instead of rebuilding it.
measures_of_success: The lookup cases pass for projects the guidance never named, and a lookup that routes from frozen rows or from a project's records alone fails them.
parameters: Where the index folder is (an environment variable, else a folder in the user's home).
inputs: A path, a project id or a request to list.
outputs: The project containing the path with its first file to read and its specifications, the ids related in a given way, or the listed ids.
effects: Writes only the index folder; makes no network call.
usage_notes: The skill's index says to read the person's local index first; the commands `esoi projects init`, `add`, `check`, `index` and `where` keep it.
selected_by: measured on the same lookup cases against the retired baseline and the floor

name: ESOI behaviour judge
scoped_purpose: Use for grading whether one reply acts by the principles when a pattern match cannot tell, and for showing how far that grading agrees with people. Avoids grading general quality and avoids being the behaviour measure itself: the judge has its own metric.
goals: Every judge is scored by its agreement with labelled replies, with false passes and false fails counted apart; the labels move from the case author's to a person's; the judge is measured again when the model behind it changes.
knowledge: Practice for model judges (agreement with human labels, preference for its own phrasing, position and length bias); the author's verdicts as the authority on what counts as acting by the principles; the case rubric of expected behaviour and failure mode.
measures_of_success: Agreement with human verdicts on held-out replies, with the two kinds of error visible, and a judge that passes everything is caught.
parameters: The judge model, the rubric and the labelled replies.
inputs: A behaviour case and one reply.
outputs: A verdict (pass or fail) and a one-line reason.
effects: A model call per reply, which costs money.
usage_notes: A sub-solution of esoi-for-ai, kept separate because its best is agreement with a human verdict, not acting by the principles (docs/explanation/esoi-for-ai.md). A behaviour score graded by a judge no person has checked is reported as such.
selected_by: the chosen way is the implementation recorded as selected; its metric is read by a person until a run measures it
gap: No reply has a person's label yet, so the judge's agreement with people is unmeasured.
action: Have a person label a sample of recorded replies, then record the judge's agreement as a run of metric-esoi-judge-agreement; review by 2026-12-31.

name: Behave by ESOI
scoped_purpose: Use for measuring, case by case, whether an AI agent's reply acts by the evolvable-structure principles, and for comparing the ways of giving an agent those principles. Avoids judging the quality of work in general and avoids rewording the principles (the author's skill is the authority).
goals: Every principle has cases, including cases of holding back and of keeping a qualifier; the recorded good replies pass and the recorded bad replies fail; every arm that calls a model is measured on the same cases and sample, inside an approved call budget.
knowledge: The author's skill, its principles and its nuance rules; the intent template; evaluation practice for language models (cases with an expected behaviour and a failure mode, a no-instructions baseline, staged samples).
measures_of_success: Offline: the recorded replies are classified as their authors meant and a keyword-stuffing baseline fails the restraint cases. Live: the skill arms pass more cases than no skill, with restraint cases passing as often as build cases.
parameters: The arm (standing instructions, on request, no skill), the model and judge model, the case subset (--sample, --only) and the call budget (--max-calls).
inputs: The rows of cases.csv, the bundled skill, and for a live arm a model command in ESOI_MODEL_COMMAND.
outputs: A reply per case, a pass or fail with a note, and a headline of passes per principle.
effects: A live arm calls a model and costs money; the offline arms call none.
usage_notes: Run reference_good and reference_bad on every change to the cases or esoi.behaviour. Run a live arm only on a decision and with approved spend (structure/metric-run-policy.md). Add a case when someone corrects an agent.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: the skill as standing instructions is how the author's skill is meant to be used, and the choice stands until a measured arm beats it
gap: The arms that call a model are not measured yet, so nothing shows how much the skill changes behaviour or which way of giving it is best.
action: Run the staged sample for each arm once Joshua approves the spend, then adopt the measured winner or declare a tie.

name: Judge ESOI behaviour
scoped_purpose: Use for grading one reply against one case when the patterns cannot tell, and for measuring how far that grading agrees with labelled replies. Avoids scoring behaviour itself (behave-by-esoi does that, with this judge's help) and avoids grading general quality.
goals: A judge is scored on a labelled good and bad reply for every case; false passes and false fails are counted apart; the share of labels that are a person's is visible; the judge prompt carries the rubric in words and never the patterns or the recorded replies.
knowledge: Practice for model judges (agreement with human labels, preference for its own phrasing, bias); the case rubric; the author's verdicts as the authority.
measures_of_success: A judge agrees with the labels on good and bad replies alike, a judge that passes everything is caught, and agreement is reported against a person's verdicts once they exist.
parameters: The judge model, the labelled replies and the human verdict column.
inputs: A behaviour case and one recorded reply.
outputs: A verdict and a reason, scored against the label.
effects: The model judge calls a model per reply, which costs money; the regex judge calls none.
usage_notes: Fill human_verdict in cases.csv to move the labels from the case author's to a person's. Regenerate cases.csv with write_cases when the behaviour cases change; a test fails until the two match.
selected_by: a declared decision pending measurement: the model judge is the only arm that can credit a reply that acts well in other words, and it is used only with its agreement shown
gap: The model judge is not measured yet and every label is still the case author's, so agreement cannot show calibration against a person.
action: Have a person fill human_verdict for a sample of replies, then run the judge on a staged sample once Joshua approves the spend.
